findings.issue_text: [BUG] app/models/user.rb:47 `validates :email, email: true` resolves top-level constant EmailValidator, but lib/validators/email_validator.rb defines Validators::EmailValidator (if reachable at all) and no top-level EmailValidator exists, so every User save/validation raises ArgumentError: Unknown validator 'EmailValidator', breaking account creation and all user-related specs

[ADVISORY] lib/validators/email_validator.rb relies on autoload/eager-load reachability never established in the diff (no require, no autoload-path change in config/application.rb, and Discourse convention is app/validators/), so environments where lib subdirectories aren't in autoload_paths get LoadError/unknown validator only at deploy time

[ADVISORY] lib/validators/email_validator.rb:18 `Regexp.new("@(#{domains})", true)` only escapes dots via gsub, leaving other regex metacharacters unescaped, and uses the deprecated boolean-flags form of Regexp.new; a site setting containing +, (, or * raises RegexpError and takes down account creation

[ADVISORY] spec/models/blocked_email_spec.rb:31 uses non-existent matcher `be_within_one_second_of` (not defined in RSpec 2 or the diff), so the spec fails with NoMethodError and the statistics-update coverage for should_block? never runs green

[ADVISORY] Ships-inert feature: nothing in this diff writes to `blocked_emails` — no admin UI, API endpoint, rake task, seed, or sync job populates the table, so the blocked email feature is dead code in production with no supported operator path to block an email

[ADVISORY] Coverage gap: the new server-to-client contract (`users_controller.rb:194-201` emitting `errors` and `values`, and `create_account_controller.js:271-279` consuming `result.errors.email && result.values`) has no test anywhere; only the model layer is tested, so regressions in the payload shape would silently disable client-side rejected-email caching
[BUG] Email matching is case-sensitive: `BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` does an exact-case lookup, so a user blocked as `spam@evil.com` can register with `SPAM@evil.com` and bypass the check

[ADVISORY] Side-effecting validation with unguarded write: `should_block?` increments `match_count`, sets `last_match_at`, and calls `record.save` from inside the User validation path even on validations that fail for other reasons or repeated signup retries, and the ignored `save` return value means race/validation failures silently drop stats writes, corrupting the observability data

[ADVISORY] Missing acceptance criterion for the user-facing message: when the server rejects the email as blocked, the client-side validation reuses the generic `user.email.invalid` string, discarding the distinct server-side `user.email.blocked` message and making that locale key unreachable through the client flow

[ADVISORY] Ships-inert feature: the entire BlockedEmail machinery (model, migration, fabricator) has no writer anywhere in the diff — no admin UI, rake task, seed, or API path inserts rows into blocked_emails, so operators cannot block any email and the feature is dead code until a follow-up lands.

[ADVISORY] Scope drift: whitelist/blacklist domain-restriction logic (email_in_restriction_setting?) was extracted verbatim from User#email_validator into a new top-level EmailValidator, not traceable to the stated intent; every model using validates :email now inherits site-wide domain policy, and these paths have zero test coverage in the diff.

[BUG] Client-side rejection reason for a blocked email uses I18n.t('user.email.invalid') ('is invalid') instead of the server's blocked message sent via result.errors; the user with a blocked address is told it's invalid and never learns their address is banned.

[ADVISORY] values: user.attributes.slice("name", "username", "email") returns more than the frontend consumes (only values.email is read); returning name and username is not traceable to any requirement and widens the response contract of a public, unauthenticated endpoint.

[ADVISORY] should_block? performs a read-modify-write (match_count += 1; save) as a side effect of validation, so the mutation happens on every validation pass including validations that never lead to a create, causing unconditional DB writes, concurrency races on match_count, and unintended persistence from any .valid? call on User.

[BUG] app/models/blocked_email.rb:12–19 — `should_block?` performs a read-modify-write (`record.match_count += 1; record.save`) inside a model validation path with no atomic update (`update_counters` / `SET match_count = match_count + 1`), so concurrent signup attempts on the same blocked email do SELECT → increment → UPDATE on a stale object and silently lose increments; every `valid?` call on any user (including controller create, uniqueness pre-checks, and repeated client submissions) fires a DB write during validation — a pure read side-effect mutates rows and breaks the validation contract (calling `user.valid?` twice double-counts and if the `save` fails the statistic is silently discarded)

[BUG] app/models/user.rb:47–48 — replacing `validates_presence_of :email` / `validates_uniqueness_of :email` with a single `validates :email, presence: true, uniqueness: true, email: true, if: :email_changed?` attaches the `if:` guard to the whole declaration, so presence and uniqueness are skipped whenever `email_changed?` is false — a pre-existing user whose email is unchanged skips uniqueness entirely, weakening the old always-run validation, and mass-update paths that don't change email lose the uniqueness guarantee

[BUG] lib/validators/email_validator.rb:12 — the blocked-email check is gated behind `record.errors[attribute].blank?`, so when a domain whitelist/blacklist error fires, `BlockedEmail.should_block?` is never called and `match_count`/`last_match_at` are not updated, silently undercounting exactly the traffic the restriction settings reject — the monitoring data the table exists to provide is wrong

[ADVISORY] db/migrate/20130724201552_create_blocked_emails.rb + app/models/blocked_email.rb — `BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` and the `UNIQUE(email)` index are case-sensitive while user emails are lowercased, so an operator-seeded row `Bad@Spam.org` never matches `bad@spam.org`, defeating the block and permitting duplicate rows differing only in case; a `lower(email)` unique index + lookup would fix this

[ADVISORY] app/models/blocked_email.rb (whole table) — nothing creates `BlockedEmail` rows (no admin UI, rake task, seed, or API writer), so the block path can never trigger in production and the 'comprehensive email validation' the PR advertises is unreachable until a separate writer ships

[ADVISORY] app/controllers/users_controller.rb:198–200 — the new `errors: user.errors.to_hash, values: user.attributes.slice(...)` payload is sent unconditionally on any create failure but the client only consults it when `errors.email` is present; the response leaks the submitted email/name back in a second shape (`values`) duplicating form state, creating two parallel representations of form state that will drift

[ADVISORY] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/create_account_controller.js:274–276 — `result.errors.email` assumes only the blocked validator produces email errors, but the domain-restriction error (`not_allowed`) also lands in `errors[:email]`; the client then permanently pushes the email into `rejectedEmails` and shows the generic `user.email.invalid` message, giving a domain-whitelist-rejected user the wrong reason with no path to clear the rejection short of page reload

[ADVISORY] Client-side rejectedEmails branch in create_account_controller.js:68–73 reuses I18n.t('user.email.invalid') for server-rejected blocked emails, discarding the new user.email.blocked message so users see the generic invalid wording instead of the distinct blocked message.

[ADVISORY] BlockedEmail#should_block? mutates persistence (increments match_count, sets last_match_at, calls save) from inside EmailValidator.validate_each, firing on every validation of any record with a changed email rather than just signup attempts, inflating and misleading match telemetry stats.

[ADVISORY] The blocked_emails table has no writer in this diff — no admin UI, API endpoint, rake task, or seed inserts rows — so the blocked-email validation feature is inert until someone hand-writes SQL, leaving the PR's stated objective unachievable by shipped operator actions.

[BUG] BlockedEmail.where(email: email) compares user-supplied email without case normalization, allowing blocked addresses to be bypassed with case variants on case-sensitive-collation DBs (Postgres), defeating the block list security control

[ADVISORY] BlockedEmail.should_block? performs a write (incrementing match_count and saving) inside a model validator, creating a write-amplification/DoS surface on the anonymous signup endpoint and corrupting the match_count statistic when validation fails for other reasons

[ADVISORY] email_in_restriction_setting? interpolates raw SiteSetting email_domains_whitelist/blacklist strings into Regexp.new with only '.' escaped, so regex metacharacters like '|', '(', '*' are interpreted as regex, allowing silent misconfiguration of the allow/deny security control

[ADVISORY] The failure response in users_controller echoes user.attributes.slice("name", "username", "email") to the anonymous client; serializing model attributes to unauthenticated JSON risks attribute disclosure if the slice list drifts to include sensitive columns — safer to re-echo request params instead

[BUG] The email_validator_spec.rb tautologically stubs BlockedEmail.should_block? and asserts the stub back, never exercising the real BlockedEmail lookup (case sensitivity, exact-match where, action_type comparison) against the validator, so regressions in the integration path pass green

[ADVISORY] Stubs scoped with .with(record.email) will cause opaque Mocha 'unexpected invocation' failures if the email argument passed to should_block? changes, testing mock wiring rather than contract

[ADVISORY] The email_in_restriction_setting? whitelist/blacklist branches of the new validator have no spec coverage; a regex escaping regression (gsub('.', '\.')) causing RegexpError would pass the suite
[ADVISORY] The spec calls validate_each directly, bypassing the if: :email_changed? conditional, so nothing tests that the validator fires only on changed emails at the production call site
[ADVISORY] The 'last_match_at is null' spec asserts a DB column default but claims an observability contract in comments that is never actually tested

[ADVISORY] should_block? couples stats update (read-modify-write match_count += 1; save) with the block decision with no spec for save-failing or concurrent paths, risking 500s on account creation instead of validation failure
[ADVISORY] The new blocked_emails table has no writer anywhere in the diff (no admin UI, API endpoint, rake task, or seed populates it), making the feature inert until a separate tool ships

[ADVISORY] BlockedEmail.should_block? performs a read-then-record.save (incrementing match_count, updating last_match_at) inside the User validation callback, adding a side-effect DB write on every validation of a user whose email changed, breaking the assumption that validation is side-effect-free and safe to retry or run read-only (spuriously incrementing stats on failed signups, seeds, imports, console checks)

[ADVISORY] should_block? does read-then-update without any lock or atomic increment, and record.save runs full validations including uniqueness on email, causing concurrent signup attempts to race on match_count increments (lost updates) and silently failing saves on case-variant email collisions while still returning true from stale in-memory state

[ADVISORY] Schema/behavior drift in user.rb validations: presence/uniqueness now run unconditionally instead of conditionally, adding an unconditional uniqueness DB query on every user save and making existing records with pre-existing duplicate emails un-updatable

[ADVISORY] EmailValidator (with BlockedEmail.should_block? DB query) runs an unconditional per-validation DB query on the signup hot path with no memoization, even on sites with no blocked_emails rows, violating the pattern of keeping validations read-free

[BUG] `should_block?` is called from `EmailValidator#validate_each` inside `user.save`'s transaction; `record.save` on the `BlockedEmail` joins that transaction, so when the user record fails validation the transaction rolls back, undoing the `match_count` increment and `last_match_at` update on every blocked signup attempt, leaving statistics permanently stale

[BUG] `record.save` (not `save!`) with the return value discarded: if the save fails (e.g., unique index race with concurrent insert of the same email), the failure is silently swallowed and `should_block?` answers from un-persisted state, with statistics writes failing silently under concurrent signups

[ADVISORY] Non-atomic read-modify-write counter: `record.match_count += 1; record.save` performs a lost-update pattern instead of an atomic `update_all("match_count = match_count + 1")`, causing undercounts when two requests validate the same blocked email concurrently

[ADVISORY] Validation with a persistent side effect: every email-changed user save performs an extra unconditional SELECT plus (on match) an UPDATE inside the validation phase, even for records that fail other validations and never persist, causing hot-path write amplification and potential statistic mutation from read-only validate-without-save code paths

[ADVISORY] Client-side `rejectedEmails` blocklist is populated only from the `create` endpoint's response, so the first submission of a blocked email always goes through the full create round-trip before rejection, and page reloads reset the list, causing repeated failed server-side create attempts

[ADVISORY] `Regexp.new("@(#{domains})", true)` builds a regexp from the raw site setting with no escaping beyond `.`, so a setting containing regex metacharacters (`(`, `+`, `[`) raises `RegexpError` during validation, making every user save with a changed email raise a 500; relocation into a shared validator widens the blast radius to any model using `validates email: true`

goldens.comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.

The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] BlockedEmail.should_block? performs a write (incrementing match_count and saving) inside a model validator, creating a write-amplification/DoS surface on the anonymous signup endpoint and corrupting the match_count statistic when validation fails for other reasons

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] BlockedEmail.should_block? performs a read-then-record.save (incrementing match_count, updating last_match_at) inside the User validation callback, adding a side-effect DB write on every validation of a user whose email changed, breaking the assumption that validation is side-effect-free and safe to retry or run read-only (spuriously incrementing stats on failed signups, seeds, imports, console checks)

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Non-atomic read-modify-write counter: `record.match_count += 1; record.save` performs a lost-update pattern instead of an atomic `update_all("match_count = match_count + 1")`, causing undercounts when two requests validate the same blocked email concurrently
